description: This is a crucial chapter in Non-Verbal Reasoning that tests visual-spatial ability. It involves analyzing the patterns formed when a transparent or opaque piece of paper is folded, cut or punched, and then unfolded.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Core logical principles governing the process of folding and unfolding paper.

key_concepts.explanation: The specific line along which the paper is folded. During the unfolding process, this line acts exactly like a flat mirror.
Unfolding the paper left-right (horizontally) creates a standard mirror image, whereas unfolding it top-bottom (vertically) creates a water image.

sections.title: Types of Questions
sections.description: Various formats of paper folding and cutting questions commonly asked in competitive exams.

results: Distinct designs or lines are drawn on a transparent square sheet.
When the sheet is folded along the given dotted line, the designs on both halves overlap to form a new combined pattern.
An opaque piece of paper is folded multiple times and finally cut or punched in a specific shape.
Upon unfolding, the cut design is repeated symmetrically across all sections of the paper based on the number of folds.

sections.title: Important Rules and Techniques
sections.description: Crucial analytical points to remember to avoid visual mistakes and enhance accuracy.

key_concepts.explanation: Always proceed in reverse order to solve the question. Unfold the very last fold first, followed by the second last, and so on.
If a cut is placed exactly on the fold line, it will form a complete symmetrical geometric figure upon unfolding (e.g., a semi-circle cut on the fold becomes a full circle).

sections.title: Steps to Solve Questions
sections.description: A systematic, step-by-step cognitive process to quickly solve paper cutting and folding questions during the exam.

steps.title: Analyze the Sequence of Folds
steps.detail: Carefully observe the direction of the provided arrows to understand the exact sequence and the axis on which the paper was folded.

steps.title: Identify the Final Cut
steps.detail: Focus closely on the exact location, angular direction, and geometric shape of the cut or punch made on the final folded portion.

steps.title: Unfold Step-by-Step
steps.detail: Mentally unfold the paper starting from the last fold. Create the corresponding mirror or water image of the cut at each step of unfolding.

steps.title: Elimination of Options
steps.detail: While predicting the complete figure, simultaneously check the given multiple-choice options. Immediately eliminate options that do not follow symmetry or do not match the fundamental shape of the original cut.
